newsitem.title: USA: SE Asia to emerge from turmoil - Templeton's Mobius.
newsitem.headline: SE Asia to emerge from turmoil - Templeton's Mobius.

text.p: Emerging markets guru Mark Mobius said Thursday South East Asian countries would eventually emerge from the turmoil of recent weeks, but that investors needed to be selective and cautious.

Mobius, president of Templeton Emerging Markets, said that Thailand, which set off the region's turmoil when it effectively devalued the baht July 2, would experience more pain, but would eventually pull out of the crisis.

"We're now going through a correction period, and international investors understand that and will eventually be back once prices reach a level that are attractive again," Mobius told Reuters Financial Television.
He said there were obvious opportunities in the Thai market, given how far prices had dropped in U.S. dollar terms, but that investors needed to be extremely careful.

"You want to be with the survivors, which means you want to be with those companies that have stronger balance sheets, that are in markets that are continuing to grow, and that have good cash flows," Mobius said of the Thai market.
He said that the Philippine and Malaysia markets may still have some ways to go down. "We feel Malaysia is rather expensive at this stage."
Other South East Asian nations seemed better able to weather the storm, Mobius said.

Any pressure on Singapore and Taiwan would likely be temporary because both countries have enormous foreign reserves, he added. Given the low interest rates and high liquidity and capital inflows in Singapore and Indonesia, he did not expect major problems.

"Generally speaking these countries have to reform their entire economies to become more competitive in view of the very low labor rates that China now offers importers all over the world," Mobius said.
